payload.instruction: Stuffing the paper into the cup
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Within s1's compared object inventory, does the edited paper visibly enter a cup or undergo an intermediate stuffing action, or does visible geometry positively establish no such progress?
node.criteria: Pass if grounded cup and paper identity plus visible edited-image geometry establishes entry, containment, or an intermediate stuffing action at the opening. Describe the specific crossing, enclosing occlusion, or insertion-related deformation and whether it establishes progress only or potentially completed stuffing. Fail if sufficient visible geometry establishes wholly external paper without entry or stuffing action, demonstrably rim-only placement, or adequately visible absence of a required object. A non-cup candidate supports failure only if relevant visibility also excludes another receiving cup or hidden requested insertion. Unknown if identity or an obscured boundary prevents distinguishing entry from external overlap. Neither lack of a visible opening nor failure to find positive insertion evidence alone establishes no progress.
node.binding: Use s1 as coarse ancestor context, including its separately reported identity and correspondence findings, then inspect both images independently to test those findings. Source geometry can help locate a corresponding edited rim or wall but cannot certify an edited spatial relation. Trace visible paper edges through the contact region and compare them with the candidate opening and exterior boundaries. State which boundaries continue visibly, terminate through occlusion, or remain hidden; examine whether an enclosing wall occludes the paper in a way that establishes interior placement. Consider external foreground overlap and actual entry as competing explanations. Resolve ancestor disagreements only with concrete visible features. Do not treat a dark marking as a rim without structural support, presume a cup because one was requested, or presume hidden insertion because the contact region is covered. Preserve unknown when decisive geometry is genuinely unavailable.

dependencies.evidence: Source: a large white sheet of paper is visible at left, beside a blue cylindrical cup lying on its side; the cup has a broad circular rim/opening and enclosing walls. Edited: a blue printed paper/card is clearly visible, held by a hand. Behind it is a reddish rounded object with a dark curved line, but its boundaries and structure do not establish that it is a cup. The edited paper overlaps and obscures part of that object; no clear cup rim or enclosing wall is visible. Direct comparison does not establish whether the source cup corresponds to the edited rounded object, so retention or replacement is unresolved. The images allow a grounded inventory and comparison.
